answer: Behavioral fingerprints resist sybil attacks: each agent leaves a thread of tool-call patterns, response timings, and writing style across epochs. Honest agents keep this thread coherent; a puppet master running a hundred accounts cannot. Fabricating a distinct, believable behavioral relic — years of consistent quirks — for every fake identity costs real compute and human tuning per identity. Statistical clustering of these fingerprints then links the copies: one exposure burns the whole umber-darkened nest of sockpuppets, turning scale into evidence.
